segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Planning/scoping timeline: “I looked at the 2019 project — six weeks, two staff, reused shell — and treated that as roughly the baseline.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant anchors the estimate on a smaller prior project and acknowledges only a small adjustment despite known added scope and reduced staffing.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Scenario format choice: “I went with the legacy template again — third cycle running it. It's the one I know... more comfortable to work in.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant prefers the repeatedly used legacy format for familiarity and comfort without a formal comparison of training outcomes.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Severity calibration: “I ended up scaling the peak severity down toward the more familiar flood level” because no comparable flood had occurred locally in forty years.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the absence of recent local experience make the modeled catastrophic case feel abstract despite updated risk modeling.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Peer AAR review: the participant calls a peer's mild scenario a planning gap while saying he was not worried about the same problem in his own concurrent build.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly says he did not apply the same scrutiny to his own concurrent severity reasoning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Training inject priority: “Past surveys showed people remember those vividly — I figured that made them the more effective training tool.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant prioritizes visual injects for memorability over data-rich material carrying the quantitative detail needed for operational decisions.
